text.p: The Federal judge hearing the proposed $1 billion settlement between Prudential Insurance Co of America and up to 10 million policy holders agreed to give lawyers another month to prepare critiques.
Judge Alfred Wolin said the so-called fairness hearing will be held February 24 instead of January 21.
The change was sought by lawyers in the class action on behalf of policy holders charging the nation's largest life insurance company with abusive sales practices that cost customers money.

Melvyn Weiss, a lead co-council for the policy holders, said the extra time was needed for the judge to consider a report that the plaintiffs' lawyers filed on Prudential's destruction of client files in its Cambridge, Mass. office.
The settlement, which could range from just over $400 million to more than $1 billion, will be offered to the 10.7 million customers who bought policies from 1982 to 1995.
The lawsuit charges that the insurance company's sales force persuaded these policy holders to increase their insurance by cashing in old policies without revealing the full costs of the transaction.
Judge Wolin conditionally approved the settlement in October, but five states, California, Flordia, Texas, Massachusetts and Virginia, withdrew from the settlement.
